scope: design review for one-time exact original modern Guest profile and local-data removal; no runtime or destructive effects
userDecision: explicit removal of the original Guest supersedes prior Guest-preservation instruction
protectedScope: all nine account profiles and their data
app-global MMKV entries and encrypted-store manifests/keys
Auth, backend, Firestore, and other external account state

decision.approach: temporary canonical router operation; no general profile-delete UI/API
requiredGuards: exact target ID hash match and modern guest kind
guest marker matches installation hash, is unbound, and is not account-bound
both SecureStore registry slots valid before mutation
global transition barrier and no pending local mutation journal
fail closed for legacy_guest or any mismatch
requiredOrdering: persist and verify a durable removal journal
create and verify a fresh guest scope
commit registry excluding old guest and selecting fresh guest
commit a second generation so both slots exclude old guest
remove only exact old modern-profile prefix keys
verify target absent, fresh guest valid, and all protected hashes unchanged
decision.recovery: block ordinary profile publication while journal is pending; resume the exact recorded operation idempotently
prohibitedMethods: clearAll or whole app data reset
direct unscoped deletion outside the canonical router
delete legacy root keys or any non-target profile prefix

capabilityProbe.method: temporary infrastructure-owned one-shot probe (no general raw-base accessor/UI); one nonce-bearing canary in an unregistered random profile namespace using the initialized native adapter; enumerate/read/remove/readback; compare protected hashes; cleanup failure stops

scores.scoreCondition: scores apply only with both-slot cleanup, durable journal, and fail-closed startup recovery

limitations: No implementation or runtime readiness is established by this review.
Fresh runtime registry kind, raw target ID hash, category baseline, and native remove capability still require verification before deletion.
The design is rejected if it updates only one registry slot or lacks journaled recovery across SecureStore/MMKV boundaries.
